---
**type 1 otic fibrocyte**

**definition**

A spiral ligament fibrocyte that underlies the stria vascularis and is part of a mesenchymal gap junction network that regulates ionic homeostasis of the endolymph. In mice, expression of connexin 26 (Gjb2) and connexin 30 (Gjb6) serves as a distinguishing molecular signature (Peeleman et al., 2020).

**type 2 otic fibrocyte**

A spiral ligament fibrocyte that is located near the spiral prominence between the basilar crest and the stria and plays an important role in potassium recycling by actively pumping K+ from the extracellular space and facilitating transcellular K+ transport through gap junctions toward Type I fibrocytes (Berrocal et al., 2008; Peeleman et al., 2020). In mice, Type II fibrocytes express connexin 26 (Gjb2) and connexin 30 (Gjb6) as part of the mesenchymal gap junction system, as well as the Na‑K‑2Cl cotransporter NKCC1 (Peeleman et al., 2020).

**type 3 otic fibrocyte**
A spiral ligament fibrocyte that is located in the deepest part of the inferior spiral ligament, directly lining the bony otic capsule. Distinguished from ion-transporting Type I and II fibrocytes, it utilises actin-myosin stress fibres and anchoring interactions to regulate basilar membrane tension. It has an elongated morphology, is most numerous in the basal, high-frequency cochlea, and expresses contractile and cytoskeletal proteins in mice, including α‑smooth muscle actin, non‑muscle myosin II, caldesmon, and the water channel Aquaporin‑1(Mahendrasingam et al., 2011; Kelly et al., 2012).

**type 4 otic fibrocyte**

A spiral ligament fibrocyte that is located in the triangular space inferior to the crista basilaris (basilar crest). This cell is spindle-shaped and expresses NKCC1 but minimal to no Na,K-ATPase (ATP1A1, ATP1B1) in mice and humans, and lacks connexin 26/30 in mice, indicating it does not participate in K⁺ recycling, unlike type II fibrocytes. Type IV fibrocyte is uniquely characterised by strong expression of connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) in mice, suggesting roles in tissue remodelling and paracrine signalling to other cochlear cells.

**type 5 otic fibrocyte**
A spiral ligament fibrocyte located in the suprastrial region above the stria vascularis, distinguished from other fibrocytes by their unique expression of COX-1 and end-foot structures that directly contact capillaries. This fibro-vascular coupling enables type V fibrocytes to regulate cochlear blood flow by translating Ca²⁺ signals into capillary vasodilation via COX-1-derived prostaglandins. This cell also participates in K⁺ recycling through high Na,K-ATPase expression in mice.
